primary_citation: 18 U.S.C. §§2701-2712 (Stored Communications Act, Title II of ECPA, Pub. L. 99-508 (1986))
short_title: Stored Communications Act — Unauthorized Access to Stored Communications; Civil Remedy $1,000/Violation
one_line_rule: Intentional unauthorized access to stored electronic communications (email, voicemail, account records) is prohibited under 18 U.S.C. §2701; civil remedy under §2707 provides the greater of actual damages or $1,000 per violation, plus punitive damages and attorneys' fees.

case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: 'Without authorization' under §2701 is broad — not limited to hacking; includes any access lacking proper authorization; stored emails after reading remain in electronic storage (backup protection prong §2510(17)(B)). Binding 9th Circuit precedent.

case_law.cite: United States v. Warshak, 631 F.3d 266 (6th Cir. 2010)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: Fourth Amendment requires search warrant for stored email regardless of age; SCA 180-day rule unconstitutional for email content; stored email has same constitutional protection as sealed postal mail; DOJ adopted national warrant policy. Persuasive authority in 9th Circuit.

sim_swap_application.phase_1_account_takeover: Using intercepted 2FA codes (SIM swap §2511) to access email accounts → reviewing stored emails, account history, communications = §2701 unauthorized access; $1,000/access event
sim_swap_application.phase_2_voicemail: Incoming calls diverted to attacker's voicemail → victim's voicemails stored on attacker's carrier/device = unauthorized access to stored voice communications = §2701; $1,000/voicemail
sim_swap_application.phase_3_account_records: Accessing account records, stored communications, financial history stored on service provider servers = §2701 unauthorized access
sim_swap_application.wiretap_boundary: Active call/SMS routing during SIM swap = §2511 ($10,000/event); stored content after access = §2701 ($1,000/event); both claims pled simultaneously for same attack sequence
sim_swap_application.ninth_circuit_advantage: Theofel (9th Cir.) applies backup protection storage broadly — virtually all content in Michael's accounts at time of compromise is §2701-protected stored communications
sim_swap_application.defendants: Ryan McClaran (primary §2701 defendant); co-conspirators who accessed accounts; AT&T (negligence enabling unauthorized access — separate tort theory)
sim_swap_application.sol: 2 years from discovery (§2707(f)); each access event = separate violation with own SOL; discovery rule tolling available
sim_swap_application.no_loss_threshold: §2707 has NO $5,000 minimum loss threshold — unlike CFAA §1030(g); $1,000 minimum applies per violation; can aggregate many violations without meeting any aggregate loss floor
